transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I keep hearing Garrett’s voice. It’s not like a memory exactly—it’s clear, like he’s standing right behind me. Sometimes it happens when I’m out on the trail, and sometimes in my painting room, which is strange because the acoustics in there are terrible, honestly, I’ve been meaning to fix that window for years.

But… yeah. Garrett is dead. I know that, part of me knows that. But when I hear him, in the moment, it feels completely real, like if I turned around fast enough he’d be there.
Besides hearing Garrett's voice, have you ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or that you're receiving special messages that others can't understand?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. “Controlled” sounds very… mechanical, like a puppet string or something, and I don’t think I’ve noticed that.

Special messages—I mean, people say things that stick with you, right? Like a line in a book or something on the radio can feel weirdly timed, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean. I tend to read into things anyway—occupational hazard, I guess. Even with my paintings, I’ll see patterns after the fact that I didn’t mean to put there.

But no, I don’t think I’ve had thoughts being controlled. I’m not sure about the special messages part. What do you mean exactly?
Have you ever had beliefs or thoughts that feel very real to you, but others might find unusual or hard to understand?

I don’t know. “Unusual” is a wide net, isn’t it? I mean, I’ve always had ideas that other people don’t quite follow at first—especially with painting, or even in psychology, people can be very literal when they want to be.

But beliefs that are… I don’t know, impossible or something? I’m not sure. Sometimes something feels meaningful in the moment and then later I think maybe I was just tired or upset. Like when you’re hiking and you see a shape in the trees and for half a second it’s a person, but then it’s just branches. Although that happens to everyone, doesn’t it?

So… I guess I’m not sure what you’re asking exactly. I don’t think I have some fixed strange belief, if that’s what you mean.
Have there been times when you believed something very strongly that turned out not to be true, and others couldn’t understand why you thought that way?

I don’t know that I can point to a clean example of that. I mean, “turned out not to be true” is tricky, isn’t it? A lot of things feel true in the moment and then later they sort of… soften.

Like, I’ve had arguments where I was absolutely convinced I understood what someone meant, and later I realized I’d built this whole structure on a tone of voice or one word. But that’s not exactly a belief-belief, it’s more like interpretation. Psychologists are terrible about that, by the way—we’re trained to listen between the lines, and then sometimes there aren’t lines there at all, just… air.

So I’m not sure. Other people have not always understood why I think the way I do, but I don’t know if that means I believed something false. I’d need an example of what you mean.
Have you ever felt like people were talking about you when they weren't, or that certain events or actions were directed at you personally, even if others didn’t see it that way?

I don’t think so—not in the sense of, like, everyone in a room secretly discussing me or the universe arranging itself around me.

I mean, I can be self-conscious. If people laugh nearby, there’s that little reflex of, “Was that me?” but I think that’s pretty normal. Or if someone posts something vague online, I might wonder for a second if it’s aimed at me, but then usually I realize I’m just filling in blanks. People are mostly thinking about themselves, honestly—which is comforting and insulting at the same time.

Events directed at me personally… I’m not sure. Sometimes coincidences feel pointed, but I don’t know that I believe they are. I tend to make meaning out of things—artists do that, therapists do that, probably grocery store managers do too in their own way. So… no, I haven’t really noticed that as a pattern.
Have there been times when you were absolutely sure something was true, even though others told you it wasn’t, and you only later realized it couldn’t have been true at all?

I’m not sure. I’m trying to think of something that fits that exactly—where I was absolutely sure, other people said no, and then later it was clearly impossible. That’s a very specific shape of thing.

I’ve definitely been stubborn. My sister would probably give you a list, honestly. There was this whole argument once about whether a restaurant used to be a pharmacy, and I was convinced because I remembered the old sign—except memory is so unreliable, isn’t it? People treat it like video, but it’s more like watercolor left in the rain.

But something that “couldn’t have been true at all”… I don’t know. I can’t think of one. I’ve had moments where I look back and think, “Why was I so certain?” but not where it was some impossible belief that everyone else was trying to talk me out of. At least not that I can clearly name right now.

Have you ever believed something that most people would consider impossible or completely outside of reality, like having special powers, being connected to events in a supernatural way, or something similar?

Special powers? No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve joked about being able to “read a room,” but that’s not supernatural—that’s just training and, honestly, sometimes anxiety wearing a blazer.

Connected to events in a supernatural way… I’m trying to think. I’ve had moments where something felt meaningful, like a song coming on at exactly the right time, or you see the same number three times and your brain wants to make a little constellation out of it. But I don’t think I believed I was causing it, or that it was some cosmic message meant only for me.

I’m not really a special powers person. If anything, I tend to over-explain things rather than mystify them. Sometimes too much. My students used to hate when I’d turn a simple question into a whole lecture about pattern recognition and confirmation bias. So… no, not that I can recall.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, especially around the time you hear Garrett’s voice?

Yeah… I mean, yes. Around then especially, but it sort of bleeds into everything.

The things that usually keep me tethered—painting, guitar, rehearsal at the theater, even work, sitting with patients and doing that careful listening thing—feel… flat. Like I can still do the motions, technically. I can hold the brush, tune the strings, show up in the room. But it’s like there’s glass between me and the part of it that used to matter.

And I hate saying that about patients, because that sounds awful. It’s not that I don’t care about people. I do. Or I remember that I do. It’s just like the meaning has gone dim, like someone turned the color saturation down on my whole life. Even things I’d normally reach for automatically feel unreachable. Like they belong to some earlier version of me who knew how to want things.
Have you had periods where you felt this way for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yeah. Yes—more than two weeks. It’s been… I’d say about four months now, the depressed, shut-down part.

It’s strange because I keep wanting to measure it by events, like “was it before that staff meeting?” or “was it when the weather changed?”—as if the weather is a medical chart. But no, it’s been most days, most of the day, for months. Around four.
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in activities you used to enjoy, like painting, playing guitar, or working with patients?

Yes. Very much so.

Painting used to be this… I don’t know, almost a place I could go. Not relaxing exactly, because I’d get obsessive about the colors, but it meant something. And guitar—same thing. I’d sit down and lose an hour without noticing. Now I pick it up and it’s like holding someone else’s instrument.

Rehearsal at the theater, too. I used to love the weird little rituals of it—the bad coffee, everyone talking over each other, someone always losing a prop. Sorry, that’s not really the point. The point is it all feels flat. Like the things that usually anchor me are still there, but I can’t reach them.

Even with patients… I show up, I can go through the motions, but it feels like I’m acting out a life that stopped meaning anything. That’s probably the part that scares me most.
